Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.messenger

Class BridgeProtocol

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.messenger.BridgeProtocol
All Implemented Interfaces:
MessengerProtocol
public class BridgeProtocol extends Object implements MessengerProtocol
A bridge backend for chat networks that require an external or native stack this project does not (and cannot reliably) bundle — XMPP, Matrix, Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal, SMS, SIP. Rather than pretend to speak the wire protocol in-process, a bridge opens the network's official client or web app (a deep link in the system browser, or an external command) and reports the hand-off honestly through the ProtocolListener.

This is the same design boundary the Video Conference app draws around WebRTC: the desktop owns the address book, the launcher and the transcript of what it can see, while the real-time session runs in the tool built for it. A bridge is non-native and advertises no MessengerProtocol.Capability.NATIVE, so the UI can label it and route "connect" to the hand-off.
